definitions.explanation: a tall structure used for surveillance, observation, or guarding an area

examples.japanese: {国境|こっきょう}に{監視塔|かんしとう}が{建|た}っている。
examples.english: A watchtower stands at the border.

examples.japanese: {刑務所|けいむしょ}の{四隅|よすみ}に{監視塔|かんしとう}が{設置|せっち}されている。
examples.english: Guard towers are placed at the four corners of the prison.

examples.japanese: ベルリンの{壁|かべ}の{跡地|あとち}には、かつての{監視塔|かんしとう}が{歴史的|れきしてき}な{記念物|きねんぶつ}として{保存|ほぞん}されている。
examples.english: At the site of the former Berlin Wall, old watchtowers are preserved as historical monuments.

notes:
Composed of {監視|かんし} (surveillance; monitoring) + {塔|とう} (tower). Refers to towers used for military, security, or correctional purposes. In historical contexts, watchtowers were used for border defense and fire detection.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {監視塔|かんしとう}を{設置|せっち}する: to install a watchtower
- {監視塔|かんしとう}から{見張|みは}る: to keep watch from a watchtower
- {監視塔|かんしとう}の{兵士|へいし}: soldier in the watchtower
- {監視塔|かんしとう}に{登|のぼ}る: to climb a watchtower

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見張|みは}り{台|だい}: lookout platform — a simpler, smaller observation point
- {展望台|てんぼうだい}: observation deck; viewing platform — for sightseeing, not security
- {物見|ものみ}やぐら: watchtower (traditional style) — a historical Japanese term for a wooden watchtower used in castles
